title: The man who saved the world. Was criticised over paperwork.
description:
Was criticised over paperwork. Accounts of how he was treated differ, but several describe a reprimand for how the incident was written up.

Duty officer at the Soviet Oko early warning centre. Shortly after midnight, the system reported a US missile launch.

Oko showed one, then four more. Petrov doubted a real attack would start with five, and the new system had not earned his trust.

Sunlight on clouds. Oko had misread sunlight reflecting off high altitude clouds as missile launches. A geostationary satellite later helped correct the error.

From a general's memoirs. The incident stayed secret until the late 1990s.

Five dots on a screen, a faulty sensor, and a man who waited for confirmation.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanislav_Petrov: read. Established 26 September 1983; Petrov as a lieutenant colonel and duty officer at the Oko early warning command centre; one missile reported with four more behind it, five in total; his reasoning (new and not fully trusted system, five seemed illogical as an opening strike, no corroboration from ground radar); the cause, sunlight aligned with high altitude clouds over North Dakota, later corrected by cross referencing a geostationary satellite; the reprimand for not describing the incident in the war diary alongside his own statement that he was neither rewarded nor punished; and that the incident became public through General Votintsev's memoirs.
- https://www.theregister.com/2017/09/18/stanislav_petrov_obit/: read. Corroborated five missiles (one, then four more), that Oko was new and buggy, that Petrov judged the US would not fire only five, that Oko was reading sunlight off the tops of heavy clouds as launches, that superiors later demoted or criticised him over paperwork, and that his role stayed secret until a Russian general's memoirs in 1997.
- https://historyrevealed.com/period/cold-war/stanislav-petrov-soviet-soldier-saved-the-world: read. Corroborated the date, shortly after midnight, five missiles reported, the sunlight on high altitude clouds explanation, that he was interrogated and reprimanded over procedure and paperwork, and that the story emerged in the late 1990s.
